items.parse_summary: A direct action question identifies the groups through the modifier “non-serving” and limits the action to the Sabbath. The choices are short alternatives with no embedded clauses.

features.required_operations: Match this group description to the passage’s two divisions going off duty, rather than those coming on duty.
features.reason: Identifying the relevant divisions is necessary to the intended assignment question; the question adds no extended reference chain.

items.parse_summary: The destination question has a subject noun phrase modified by “in the tower of Shechem”; within that modifier, “of Shechem” identifies the tower. The location identifying the leaders must be distinguished from the destination they entered.

features.quote: the leaders in the tower of Shechem
features.required_operations: Attach “in the tower” to the leaders and “of Shechem” to the tower, then identify the separate destination requested by “Where.”
features.reason: The compact modifier identifies the intended leaders and preserves the distinction between their identifying location and their destination.

items.parse_summary: A main outcome question contains one temporal clause naming the man of God as the person praying. The options name different affected entities; the target option uses a passive restoration clause.

features.quote: What happens when the man of God prays?
features.required_operations: Distinguish the person praying from the king whose hand is restored, and interpret the passive wording in option D.
features.reason: The intercessor–beneficiary distinction is part of the intended event relationship, not avoidable structural elaboration.

items.parse_summary: A direct action question uses “non-serving” to identify the groups and “on the Sabbath” to specify the time. There are no embedded clauses.

features.required_operations: Connect this description to the two divisions going off duty, distinguishing them from those coming on duty.
features.reason: This identification is necessary to retrieve the intended guarding assignment.

items.parse_summary: The outcome question contains a temporal clause whose subject is the seven exorcists; “tried” takes the infinitival action “to cast out,” modified by “in the name of Jesus.” Option B coordinates an attack with the victims’ subsequent flight.

features.quote: The evil spirit beat them and they fled
features.required_operations: Track the evil spirit as the attacker, resolve “them” to the seven exorcists, and retain that group as the subject of “they fled.”
features.reason: The subject change expresses the two components of the intended outcome: attack and flight.

items.parse_summary: The question embeds the Levite’s prospective inquiry inside Dan’s people’s desire: they want the Levite to ask God something. Each substantive option supplies an indirect yes/no question, with “they” referring to the travelers.

features.quote: What do Dan's people want the Levite to ask God?
features.required_operations: Separate the people’s request from the inquiry the Levite is to address to God, then identify that inquiry’s content.
features.reason: The nested request and inquiry are the intended semantic relationship.

features.required_operations: Read the option as the content of “ask God” and resolve “they” to Dan’s people rather than the Levite.
features.reason: The short reference connects the requested inquiry to the travelers whose success is at issue.

items.parse_summary: A direct question asks for Zebul’s characterization of an identified group. The choices are short descriptions; the respondent must distinguish his characterization from what the approaching figures actually were.

features.quote: How did Zebul describe the men?
features.required_operations: Retrieve Zebul’s description rather than report the narrator’s identification or Gaal’s observation.
features.reason: Attributing the description to Zebul is central to the intended target.

features.required_operations: Connect the definite noun phrase to the approaching people discussed by Gaal and Zebul.
features.reason: This is a short, necessary reference to the group being characterized.

items.parse_summary: A single main clause asks for the captain’s response, with “to the plan” specifying what prompted it. Neither the question nor any choices introduce embedded clauses.

features.required_operations: Treat the definite noun phrase as the antecedent event prompting the captain’s response and distinguish it from the orders he subsequently gives.
features.reason: The question contains only a short backward reference, without an extended chain or nested setup.

items.parse_summary: A main outcome question contains one temporal clause, “after the man of God leaves.” The temporal clause establishes the event after which the requested outcome occurs, with no additional embedding.
A direct why-question asks for the purpose of the Levite’s departure from Bethlehem. It has one participant, one departure event, and no embedded clause or reference chain.
A direct how-question asks which action constituted Uzziah’s trespass against Yahweh. Uzziah is the actor and Yahweh is the party against whom the act is characterized; there is no clause embedding.

A direct why-question asks for the cause of the descendants’ search for territory. The substantive options are separate causal propositions; option A expresses the absence of an inheritance up to the relevant time.

features.quote: They had not yet received an inheritance among Israel's tribes
features.required_operations: Interpret “not yet” as negating receipt of an inheritance through the relevant time, rather than expressing permanent exclusion.
features.reason: The temporal negative directly expresses the intended reason for seeking territory and does not involve interacting negatives.
